headline_marked: Two [[Singapore deportees remanded over suspected militancy]]
headline: Two Singapore deportees remanded over suspected militancy
summary: Sahedul Islam and Rishad Ali were sent back to Bangladesh by Singaporean authorities after being arrested for suspected links to banned militant groups.
details: A Dhaka court has granted a three-day remand for Sahedul Islam (37) and Rishad Ali (25), who were deported from Singapore on suspicion of militancy.
The two men were handed over to Dhaka airport immigration police on Wednesday after being arrested by Singaporean police for suspected ties to banned militant organizations.
Police requested a five-day remand, stating that the suspects admitted during initial questioning that they were involved with banned militant groups while in Singapore.
Authorities believe the suspects could potentially carry out attacks in Bangladesh or other countries and are investigating their funding sources and local connections.
During the court hearing, Rishad Ali claimed he was arrested in Singapore for writing a Facebook post about a person named Farabi, a leader of Hefazat-e-Islam.
Police have seized three mobile phones and passports from the suspects as part of the ongoing investigation.
caption:
Two men deported from Singapore for suspected militancy are now in police remand in Dhaka.

A Dhaka court has granted a three-day remand for Sahedul Islam (37) and Rishad Ali (25), who were deported from Singapore on suspicion of militancy.

The two men were handed over to Dhaka airport immigration police on Wednesday after being arrested by Singaporean police for suspected ties to banned militant organizations.

Police requested a five-day remand, stating that the suspects admitted during initial questioning that they were involved with banned militant groups while in Singapore.

Authorities believe the suspects could potentially carry out attacks in Bangladesh or other countries and are investigating their funding sources and local connections.

During the court hearing, Rishad Ali claimed he was arrested in Singapore for writing a Facebook post about a person named Farabi, a leader of Hefazat-e-Islam.

Police have seized three mobile phones and passports from the suspects as part of the ongoing investigation.

headline_marked: Verdict in 25 days: [[3 get death penalty]] for rape and murder of 5-year-old
headline: Verdict in 25 days: 3 get death penalty for rape and murder of 5-year-old
summary: A Mymensingh court sentenced three men to death and a juvenile to 12 years in prison for the brutal killing of a young girl.
details: A court in Mymensingh has sentenced three people to death for the rape and murder of a five-year-old girl in Dhobaura upazila. A juvenile court separately sentenced a fourth accused, who was a minor at the time of the crime, to 12 years and six months in prison.
The convicts are identified as Arif (19), Rakib (21), and Sayem (19). The juvenile convict was 17 years old at the time of the crime.
The victim went missing from near her home on June 14. Her body was later discovered on the bank of the Kansa river in the upazila.
The victim's father filed a rape and murder case with Dhobaura Police Station the following day. Police arrested the four accused and submitted the charge sheet within nine days.

The entire trial was completed within 25 days of the case being filed. Mymensingh SP Mohammad Kamrul Hassan stated that the investigation was expedited due to the prompt delivery of autopsy and DNA reports.
caption:
Justice delivered in just 25 days. Three men sentenced to death for the rape and murder of a 5-year-old girl.

A court in Mymensingh has sentenced three people to death for the rape and murder of a five-year-old girl in Dhobaura upazila. A juvenile court separately sentenced a fourth accused, who was a minor at the time of the crime, to 12 years and six months in prison.

The convicts are identified as Arif (19), Rakib (21), and Sayem (19). The juvenile convict was 17 years old at the time of the crime.

The victim went missing from near her home on June 14. Her body was later discovered on the bank of the Kansa river in the upazila.

The victim's father filed a rape and murder case with Dhobaura Police Station the following day. Police arrested the four accused and submitted the charge sheet within nine days.

The entire trial was completed within 25 days of the case being filed. Mymensingh SP Mohammad Kamrul Hassan stated that the investigation was expedited due to the prompt delivery of autopsy and DNA reports.
